The BNP is treading the path of fascism by politicizing administrative positions; the Jamaat-e-Islami Amir is set to participate in discussions on November 7th; processions will be held tomorrow across Dhaka and the rest of the country, announced Rizvi.

snippet.title: LAS NOTICIAS: Trump se lleva un mazazo inesperado, Marco Rubio rompe su silencio y bolsas en pánico
snippet.description:
LAS NOTICIAS: Trump se lleva un mazazo inesperado, Marco Rubio rompe su silencio y bolsas en pánico

Jornada de máxima tensión internacional con múltiples focos de crisis que sacuden la geopolítica y los mercados financieros globales. Estados Unidos se sitúa al borde de una nueva ofensiva militar de gran intensidad contra objetivos estratégicos y nucleares en Irán: el Pentágono altera los planes del secretario de Defensa, Pete Hegseth, mientras Irak decreta la alerta por riesgo radiológico fronterizo, restringe su espacio aéreo y se detectan movimientos navales sospechosos junto a cables submarinos de telecomunicaciones en el golfo de Omán.

En Washington, la Administración Trump se enfrenta a un terremoto político sin precedentes tras el revés electoral en las elecciones de mitad de mandato. Ted Cruz califica la derrota como un nuevo 'Watergate', se desatan pugnas internas en torno a la sucesión hacia 2028 con Marco Rubio y Pete Hegseth resistiendo en sus cargos. Paralelamente, Donald Trump revela conversaciones con Moscú para un acuerdo global sobre Europa y Ucrania, mientras en Israel se acelera la pugna por el poder entre Gadi Eisenkot y Benjamín Netanyahu.

En el terreno económico, los mercados financieros sufren un viernes negro con ventas masivas en Wall Street: el Dow Jones se desploma 1.833 puntos y el Nasdaq cae un 6,4% arrastrado por el pánico regulatorio sobre la inteligencia artificial y los semiconductores. Además, analizamos el caso Koldo en España con nuevas detenciones de la UCO, el choque diplomático entre Javier Milei y Pedro Sánchez en Madrid, y la incertidumbre bancaria en Paraguay. snippet.title: Bishop Calls His Wife a Thief From the Pulpit, Not Knowing the Church Sits on Her Land | Full Movie
snippet.description:
"In this house, you call me Bishop." Welcome to the full drama movie: HOLY GROUND.

Sunday morning in Houston. In front of three hundred church members, Bishop Lionel Batiste points down from the pulpit at his own wife: somebody stole 1.2 million dollars from the building fund, and the transfers came from her phone. Then his young secretary Shayla walks out of the side door and stands at his side, wearing the pearl earrings that belonged to the First Lady's late mother. That same afternoon, the locks on the parsonage are changed, and the pregnant secretary is standing in LaTonya's doorway.

But LaTonya Batiste teaches math for a living, and numbers don't lie. The money left the account while she was asleep on an operating table, and only one person was holding her phone. And there is something nobody in that church knows: the ground under the building belongs to her. Her daddy only leased it to the church for one dollar a year. The Bishop is secretly selling it to a Dallas developer for nine million dollars.

A credit union log, a nurse who saw everything, a new house in Missouri City, a fake fall in the fellowship hall, an arrest on Thanksgiving Eve, a letter hidden for twenty years, and a baby that can't be his. Every receipt leads back to the pulpit.

Watch the full movie for the ultimate karma: a land deal torn in half in front of the whole church, a lapel mic that recorded every word, a Bishop on his knees in the center aisle, a gold ring dropped into the offering plate "for the building fund", handcuffs on anniversary Sunday, letters from the county jail thrown away unopened, and a First Lady who walks out into the sunlight and never looks back.

Daddy built a church. She built a life.

snippet.title: What Happens To A Pill After You Swallow It?
snippet.description:
Be honest: do you swallow your pills dry? Yes or no? 👇

You swallow a painkiller for your headache, and you think it goes straight to your head. It doesn't. First, it has to survive a trip through your whole body.

Second zero: your tongue pushes it back and a wave of muscle squeezes it down your esophagus. A few seconds later it drops into your stomach. Minute two: the hidden trick kicks in. The pill is packed with a disintegrant, a powder that soaks up water like a sponge and swells until the tablet bursts apart from the inside. Chunks, then grains, then dust, and the drug dissolves into your stomach fluid.

Minute fifteen: it slides into your small intestine, a tube lined with millions of tiny fingers called villi. That's where it really gets in, right through the wall and into your blood. But that blood doesn't go to your head. It goes to your liver first, through the portal vein. Your liver doesn't care that it's medicine. To its enzymes it's a foreign chemical, so they start tearing it apart. With some drugs, the liver destroys almost all of it. That's why heart patients put nitroglycerin under the tongue: swallowed, the liver would wipe it out.

Your painkiller is tougher. Minute thirty: what's left gets pumped through your heart to every corner of your body. It has no idea where your headache is. It's simply everywhere, and the pain starts to fade. Hours later, your liver and kidneys clear out the rest. Yes, through your pee.

One catch: swallow a pill dry or lying down, and it can get stuck in your esophagus and burn a sore right into the wall. Take pills upright, with a full glass of water.

Sources: standard pharmacology of tablet disintegration (superdisintegrants), intestinal absorption and the first-pass effect (portal vein, hepatic CYP450 enzymes); oral bioavailability of nitroglycerin ( less then 1 %) vs. ibuprofen/paracetamol (high); pill-induced esophagitis.

This video is for education, not medical advice. Always follow the instructions on the package or from your doctor or pharmacist.
